subject: XFN readout: QBR readiness, exec asks & action slate
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Sarah Connors <sarah@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: XFN readout: QBR readiness, exec asks & action slate

Team —

Quick readout from this morning's customer QBR prep with Acme Analytics and our execs. There are three things we need to lock this week so the customer-facing slate and the exec deck are aligned: 

1) Pricing contingency and a short-term SLA ask from Acme (they want a 95th %-ile latency SLO for two endpoints for the pilot). Owner: Marissa — can you confirm if we can scope a temporary SLA on Dedicated capacity and the delta in pricing?

2) Rollout gating for the new quantization profile (vQ2) — Ops risk noted: we need a fallback plan if quality regression is observed on long-form prompts. Owner: Vivek — propose rollback + soft-launch policy and an instrumentation checklist.

3) Exec one-pager and ask framing — product needs two bullets: (a) clear customer value (latency/cost delta + core use case) and (b) three toggles we will offer the customer during pilot. Owner: Lauren + me — I drafted a one-pager (attached) but need a tightened narrative for the exec slide.

Action summary and deadlines (please treat as hard):
- Marissa: SLA feasibility + delta pricing and short note to ProcureOps by EOD Wed (2028-06-20).
- Vivek: Rollout/rollback checklist and instrumentation table by Thu noon (2028-06-21).
- Lauren/Karthik: Finalize exec one-pager and 2-slide ask for Friday 10:00 PT (2028-06-22).

Attachments: QBR_prep_one-pager.pdf (draft), MA_pacing_sheet.xlsx (current pacing numbers).

Notes from the call: Acme is sensitive to cost but will pay premium for consistent latency for their analytics pipeline. They expect a formal procurement timeline after the executive readout, so procurement coordination (ProcureOps) is likely this week.

Please reply with any blockers. If something is slipping, call it out now so we can escalate.

Thanks —
Karthik
Head of Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Sarah Connors <sarah@acmeanalytics.com>, ProcureOps <procure@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 11:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: XFN readout: QBR readiness, exec asks & action slate

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear asks. Quick take on SLA/pricing:
- We can scope a 95th %-ile latency SLO for the two endpoints on a Dedicated pool for the pilot window, but it requires a 3-month reserved commitment (shorter reserve increases unit pricing ~18%).
- If we keep a flexible commit (monthly reserved with a 30-day termination), procurement will push back. ProcureOps (cc'd) — can you confirm acceptable commitment lengths?

Proposed near-term options (pick one):
A) 3-month reserved pool + 10% pilot premium — simplest for Ops and SLO guarantees.
B) Monthly reserved with 30-day notice + 18% premium — more expensive but flexible for Acme.

I'll draft the pricing delta and put an options table in ProcureOps' thread by EOD Wed. Also, I need Vivek to confirm whether Dedicated pool scaling (burst headroom) is required for the SLA or whether caching/batching suggestions suffice.

Marissa
Senior Account Manager, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com>

Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 13:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: XFN readout: QBR readiness, exec asks & action slate

Marissa / Team —

I can own the rollout gating documentation. High level:
- Soft-launch approach: enable vQ2 for 10% of traffic on a canary Dedicated node group with realtime quality checks against our prompt set (we'll use the MA_pacing_sheet prompts + two long-form tests).
- Fallback: instant routing to vQ1 (current profile) + kill-switch at the gateway. Expected failover < 250ms to avoid visible degradation.
- Instrumentation: per-request KV cache hit, per-token latency, and a similarity-based quality score computed from the eval harness. I'll publish an instrumentation table to the Drive link by Thu 12:00 PT.

Ops notes for procurement: if we need burst capacity >20% above steady-state, we should add a 10% buffer to the reserve estimate. That ties to the SLA math Marissa is putting together.

I'll prepare the checklist and a short runbook (INF-4921) and ping the gateways team for the kill-switch hook.

—Vivek
VP, Inference Ops
Redwood Inference

All — thanks for the quick turn. Short update for the exec thread: 

1) Marissa: target EOD Wed for the pricing options is fine. Please include a redline showing the committed reserve length impact and a one-line recommended option.
2) Vivek: your canary + kill-switch approach is exactly what execs want to see. Please include the worst-case failover latency number in the doc (you mentioned <250ms — confirm measured baseline).
3) Karthik/Lauren: I'll take the draft one-pager and trim to two bullets + an ask slide. I'll drop the final 2-slide pack to the Drive folder and reply-all with the link by Thu 9:00 PT so the execs have time to review.

Exec ask phrasing (proposal):
- "Approve pilot: Dedicated reserved pool (3 months) + SLA commitment for two endpoints — support a phased vQ2 roll-out with automatic fallback to vQ1 if quality dips."
- "Authorize procurement pathing and enable a 10% burst buffer for pilot capacity."

If nobody flags blockers by EOD Wed I'll move these into the exec packet. Small remaining questions: Marissa — will ProcureOps need a signed MSA amendment for a 3-month reserve? ProcureOps (cc'd) — quick confirmation appreciated.

Lauren
Director, Product Marketing
Redwood Inference
